title: I Logged Every Pottery-Kiln Slot My Studio Mate Called Overflow

parts.text: I glazed at 8:06 a.m. and the kiln whiteboard already had my mate's name in every cone-6 square. The booking sheet she posted said: ONE SHELF PER MEMBER. OVERFLOW GOES TO WAITLIST. I was thirty-three, evening member, holding mugs that had dried on time. Lena said, "Overflow is a vibe, not a list." I pointed at her sheet. She shrugged. "I keep the kiln alive." I photographed the board, the sheet, and my dry mugs. Then I logged every extra square as a waitlist steal in the studio book. At 8:14 the owner asked why Lena's name filled a steal report.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see every cone-6 square named Lena against her one-shelf sheet.

social.video_title: She called every kiln square overflow — Part 1/2
social.description: Dry mugs, a whiteboard of one name, and a sheet she posted. I logged the steals. Would you have unfired your week?

parts.text: Lena called it heat management until the firing invoice showed empty member shelves. I printed the report, the sheet, and the photo. My mugs went in. Lena paid an extra firing and told the studio the sheet was always about optics. Optics is a word potters use when a whiteboard exists. Kiln policy now has a second line: VIBES ARE NOT A WAITLIST. I keep one shelf. Lena waitlists. The kiln hums like it finally got a queue.

social.video_title: Vibes are not a kiln waitlist — Part 2/2
social.description: Steal report, extra firing fee, and a second line on the sheet. Was heat ever every square?
